h: Disputes and Invoices status weren't staying in sync

Looked closely at "I just deleted a dispute, but it reappeared" using the attached sync log. The log's only db:leaseDisp entry around that time is the delete itself going out cleanly (30 -> 29 records, nothing flagged as dropped) -- there's no later entry in this log showing the record coming back, so it did not resurface on this computer by any mechanism this log can see. The most likely explanation is a second device or browser tab that still had the old copy of that dispute and pushed its own save after the delete went out -- the sync logic currently can't always tell "a genuinely new record" apart from "a device's stale copy of something deleted elsewhere," so in that specific race it can re-add it. A real fix needs a small synced list of deleted-dispute IDs so every device recognizes a deletion no matter which device made it or what order the saves arrive in -- that's a real change worth doing carefully rather than rushing in, so it is not included in this build. If it happens again, checking whether another computer/tab had Disputes open around the same time would help confirm this.

h: Fixed invoice status overrides (and other per-line edits) getting silently reverted, and hardened cloud sync against losing whole records

i.x: Marking an invoice line's status Completed/OK (or Review/Issue) in Fleet > Invoices could get silently reverted back to its automatic status later -- 285863 and others. Root cause: when the cloud sync compares your invoice against anyone else's save of that same invoice, it was treating all of that invoice's line items as one single all-or-nothing block. So if someone else so much as touched a totally different line on the same invoice (a note, an amount, anything) around the same time, the sync would keep their entire set of lines and quietly throw away yours -- including a status you'd manually set, even though the two edits never actually touched the same line. Line edits are now merged line-by-line (matched by unit number), so your status override on one line can no longer be wiped out by someone else's unrelated edit to a different line on the same invoice.

Also hardened the same cloud-merge logic for the rare case where it can't confidently match up which records on two devices are "the same one" (for example if a record is missing the field normally used to tell them apart). Previously it played it safe by falling back to just pushing your own copy over whatever was on the server -- which is exactly backwards, since that's the one situation where it's least sure what the server has that you don't, and that uncertainty is itself a way a just-added record could get wiped out. It now keeps everything already on the server and adds anything of yours that isn't already there, instead of ever replacing the server's data outright in that situation.

Also looked into the 7 missing invoices (YR5227, YR5230, YR5231, YU5330, YV3892, YV3894, YV3897). The sync log on this computer shows the count going cleanly from 94 to 101 (all 7 added successfully) at 8:02:58 AM Eastern on 11/24, staying at 101 through 8:03:59 AM, then showing up already back at 94 by 8:04:07 AM -- with no deletion and no error recorded on this computer in between. That means this computer did not do the push that removed them; it only received the already-reduced count, most likely from another computer or tab that pushed a stale copy of the invoice list in that same window. If another computer had Invoices open around 8:03 AM Eastern that morning, its own sync log (Management -> Logs) would help pin down exactly what happened -- happy to take a look if you can grab it. The 7 invoices need to be re-uploaded either way -- they're not recoverable from this end.

h: Fixed the remaining window-opening inconsistencies: border, start point, and content size now always match between windows

i.x: Found the real cause behind Truck Database's window acting different from Work Orders and most other windows when it opened: a handful of windows (Truck Database, PTI, Chains, Ready Units, and several others) are resized to their real final size in a second step, right after they're first created, instead of being created at that size directly. The opening animation used to measure the window before that second resize happened, so it built its whole reveal -- the border, the growing frame, the content -- around the smaller, temporary size, then the real size snapped in moments later once the resize caught up. That's what showed up as a border that looked incomplete at first, a window that seemed to jump instead of smoothly growing from its button, and text/tables that looked briefly oversized before shrinking. The animation now waits one frame -- about 1/60th of a second, not noticeable -- so it always measures the window's true final size before building the reveal, no matter which path created that window. Every window now opens the same reliable way, with nothing after this to catch up or correct mid-animation.

A second, separate bug meant the button-to-window connection added a couple of updates ago could get silently dropped partway through the chain of internal logic that decides what happens when a window opens -- so quite a few windows still fell back to guessing where to start from instead of using the exact button you clicked, which is why some still looked like they opened from the middle of the screen. This is the same shared opening/closing mechanism as the last few updates, not a special case for Truck Database -- so every other window that had the same two bugs (several other Fleet Hub, Safety, and HR windows) is corrected along with it, with nothing else about how any of them work or look changed.

h: Narrowed the window where a completed work order could silently flip back to Open

This closes the gap down to the brief round trip of each individual save, which is a meaningfully smaller window than before, but it is not a guarantee against every possible cause -- in particular it cannot undo or prevent a database fix script being run with outdated data in it. The two work orders that reappeared need to be checked directly in the database to confirm they are fully corrected and to see whether the same stray-broadcast pattern is what hit them.

h: Reworked the window-opening animation: content can no longer stretch, and it now starts from the actual button you clicked more reliably

i.x: The last couple of updates animated windows by resizing the real window element (with a counter-adjustment meant to keep its contents looking normal). In practice that was still risky -- it depended on nothing inside ever fighting that resize, and real screens are complicated enough that it could still show stretched or oversized content in some cases. The window's content is now never resized or distorted in any way, under any circumstance -- it's revealed at its true, normal size as the window opens, the same way a shade or curtain reveals what's already there, rather than anything being stretched into place.

Where the opening animation starts from was being tracked with a fairly narrow, hand-picked list of button types, which missed some real buttons and rows in the app -- that's why some windows opened connected to the button you clicked while others seemed to just appear in the middle of the screen. That tracking is now far more general, so it correctly finds the actual clicked button, icon, or row in many more places throughout the app.

This still is not a literal curved/warped animation like some operating systems do for minimizing a window -- that effect relies on the operating system being able to bend the window's actual pixels as a flexible image, which a live, still-interactive web page genuinely cannot do without freezing its content into a picture first (which would bring back the earlier blank-placeholder problem). What this update delivers instead is a window that visibly, reliably grows out of the exact button you clicked, with its real content never distorted along the way.

h: Fixed two real data-loss bugs: a completed work order could flip back to Open, and a large attachment could vanish after uploading

i.x: A direct database correction (like the Truck/Trailer labeling fix) updates a work order's row without necessarily changing its own internal timestamp. That row still gets broadcast live to every signed-in device the instant it's touched -- and until now, every field in that broadcast was applied without question, even when it was older than what was already on screen. That is how a work order that had just been marked Completed could flip back to Open with nobody touching it: the broadcast carried a stale snapshot. The live feed now only applies a row when it's actually newer than what's already there; a stale or out-of-order broadcast is ignored instead of overwriting the screen.

Any attachment over about 15-20KB (roughly anything that isn't a tiny thumbnail -- so most photos, scans, and PDFs) is meant to get copied to separate file storage, with only a small placeholder kept in the main record to save space. If that copy step ever failed for any reason -- a brief network hiccup, the file-storage service being briefly unavailable -- the attachment was still fully intact in the main database, but the app would still swap in the placeholder locally as if the copy had succeeded, with nothing left anywhere to get the real file back from. That is almost certainly what happened to the inspection attachment that disappeared. The placeholder swap now only happens once the copy has actually been confirmed successful -- if it fails, the full attachment stays right where it already safely is instead of being replaced with an empty placeholder.

The specific attachment already affected by this needs a one-time manual recovery since it already got swapped locally before this fix existed -- see the message from support for how that's being handled. Going forward, this can't happen again.

h: Deep sync audit: fixed a real new-storage save race, cleaned up a wasteful resave, sped up Driver saves

i.x: The new per-work-order table (added in 1.0.765) could silently drop a save if it landed at almost the exact same moment as someone else's save to the same work order -- no error, no notice, just quietly not saved to that table (your change was always still safe in the main storage either way, so nothing was ever truly lost, but it could look like a save "didn't stick" on that device until the next sign-in). It now automatically retries a few times within a fraction of a second, which resolves essentially every case; if it still can't after repeated genuine conflicts, you now get a clear notice instead of silence.

A background mileage-snapshot check (runs every 2 minutes for every signed-in user) had the same text-comparison mistake fixed in several other spots a few updates ago, causing a pointless resave every single time even with no real change. Harmless, just wasteful -- fixed.
Saving, deleting, or uploading a document for a Driver now pushes to the cloud immediately, matching the instant-save behavior already in place for Work Orders, Trucks, Trailers, and other records.

This was a full audit of the save-and-sync engine after the last few fixes, specifically looking for the same mistakes elsewhere before they could cause another report like today's. Everything else checked out clean.

h: Fixed: Unit Type was locked/grayed out on a brand new Work Order before you'd even picked a unit

i.x: Unit Type is meant to lock only once you've picked a real unit, or when you're editing a work order that already existed before today -- so you can't accidentally switch an existing truck work order to Trailer (or back) after the fact. A brand new work order's auto-saving draft was being internally treated the same as 'already existed,' so Unit Type was locking immediately on a new work order, before any unit was chosen, blocking you from switching it off the tab's default.
Unit Type still locks, same as before, once you pick a real unit number, or when genuinely editing a pre-existing work order. This only unblocks a brand new, still-empty work order.

h: Fixed: trailer work orders were showing up as trucks after the new table system switched on

i.x: The new per-work-order table added in 1.0.765 was missing a column for whether a work order belongs to a Truck or a Trailer. Every work order read back from that table was silently defaulting to Truck -- which is why trailer work orders appeared to vanish from the Trailers tab. Nothing was deleted; they were only being mislabeled the instant they were read. A one-time database fix restores the correct Truck/Trailer label on every existing work order from your real, untouched data.
No screens or buttons changed. This only restores the correct Truck/Trailer grouping going forward and for everything already entered.

h: Check for updates no longer shows a confusing version number next to the title bar

i.x: The version shown next to the app title (top bar) updates itself the instant a fix is published, with no install needed. "Check for updates" was checking something different: the installed program itself, which only changes when a real new version is built and installed. Those two numbers were never meant to be the same thing, but showing only one bare number next to "up to date" made it look like a mismatch or a bug.

"Check for updates" now clearly labels both numbers side by side -- "Program version" and "App content" -- with a short note that it's normal for them to differ. The program version only moves when you actually install a new version; the content version moves automatically and doesn't need an install.

h: Work orders now save one at a time in a dedicated table, instead of all sharing one record per company

i.x: Every work order for a company used to live inside one single shared record, all bundled together -- any save of any work order rewrote that whole bundle. Work orders now each get their own individual row in the database. This is the main reason two people editing work orders around the same time could ever collide in the first place; with each work order fully separate, that category of collision mostly goes away by itself. Nothing else about how Work Orders looks or behaves changes -- same screens, same buttons, same numbering.

Fixed an old, unrelated crash hit while preparing this: signing in under a company with no saved company profile could throw an error partway through sign-in. Every real company already has a profile, so this never came up before; fixed to fall back safely like every other spot in the app already does.

Your other data -- drivers, trailers, loads, citations, inspections, everything except work orders -- is not part of this change and keeps working exactly as it does today. Nothing in the old storage was deleted; it stays in place as a safety net.

h: Internal: the new work-order table system can now only ever switch on per company, never for everyone at once

i.x: No visible changes for anyone. This is behind-the-scenes groundwork for the new per-record work order storage being built and tested (still completely off for every real company). It used to be controlled by one single on/off switch for the whole app; it's now a list of specific companies, starting with just the throwaway test company, so turning it on for testing can never accidentally affect Westmore, Straight2IT, or anyone else. A real company only ever gets added to that list on purpose, after review and a scheduled changeover window.

h: Fixed the same root cause in several other places, after finding it affects more than just the search box

i.x: The last update traced the Truck Services search-box issue to comparing two records by converting them to text instead of comparing their actual values -- text built that way can come out different purely from which order the fields happen to be in, even when nothing really changed, and a record read back from the cloud can have its fields rearranged that way. Went through the rest of the app looking for every other place that compares records the same fragile way, since the same cause could be showing up elsewhere without an obvious keystroke to blame.

Found it in the core engine that combines your changes with everyone else's when you're not the only one editing. In rare cases this could make a device think its own work order had collided with a different one on the same number -- renumbering it and showing a 'created on another device' notice -- when really it was just seeing its own record reflected back with its fields rearranged. It could also log a same-field 'double-edit' notice for a field nobody actually double-edited. Both are now compared by actual content, not text.

Found the same issue in three smaller spots: the Company Home dashboard's CSA history snapshot (could re-save on every visit to that screen even with nothing new), the Management -> Storage 'Recover missing data' tool (could duplicate a record under a new number even if the backup and the current copy were identical), and the FMCSA crash-import counter (could miscount an unchanged crash as 'updated').

No visual changes. This is the same kind of fix as the last update, applied everywhere else the same mistake was made, so a device can't falsely think something changed -- and can't falsely act on it -- just because the cloud rearranged a record's fields.

h: Fixed: typing in the Truck/Trailer Services search box triggered a sync on every keystroke

i.x: Opening Truck Services or Trailer Services re-checks that each unit's completed-service history matches its completed work orders, and saves a correction immediately if it finds one (added last update, on purpose, so a real correction can't silently disappear). That check compares the stored entries against freshly recomputed ones by converting both to text -- but text built that way can come out slightly different purely because of which order the fields happen to be arranged in, even when every value is identical. A completed entry that had been saved to the cloud and read back could come back with its fields rearranged that way, which made the check wrongly think something had changed on every single comparison -- including every time the screen re-displays while you're typing in that window's search box, since typing re-displays it. That's what was showing up as a sync firing on every keystroke.
The check now compares the actual field values directly instead of relying on their arrangement, so it only saves a correction when something genuinely changed.
The correction-gets-saved-immediately behavior from last update is untouched for real mismatches -- this only stops it from falsely triggering on every keystroke.

h: Fixed: completing a work order didn't actually get the instant-sync speedup from the last update

i.x: This app has several layers of patches built up over time, and the instant-sync change from the last update reached the ORIGINAL version of a few actions — but Complete Work Order, Reopen Work Order, Add Service Line, Set Status, and Create Settlement had each since been replaced by a newer version that never called back to it. So those specific actions were quietly still running on the slower, original short delay the whole time, not the instant push. They're now wired up correctly, for real this time.

Found a second, related issue causing completed work orders' service history to look like it vanished from a truck or trailer's record: opening Truck Services or Trailer Services double-checks that each truck's history matches its completed work orders, and silently patches it on screen if it finds a mismatch — but it was never actually saving that patch. So the fix could look right for a moment and then disappear again the next time anything synced, because the correction never stuck. It now saves and pushes that correction immediately when it makes one.

No visual or workflow changes — same buttons, same screens. This only fixes which actions actually get the instant push, and makes the truck/trailer history check durable instead of silent and temporary.

h: Pressing Save, Complete, or Delete now pushes to the cloud immediately, no waiting

i.x: Saving, completing, or deleting a record — a work order, inspection, driver, trailer, citation, invoice, settlement, or anything else — now starts sending to the cloud the instant you press the button, instead of waiting out the usual short delay that's there to batch up rapid background saves while you're typing. That background delay (about 0.2 seconds) still applies while you're actively typing in a draft, so typing itself doesn't flood the connection — this only speeds up the moment you actually commit something.
There's still the real time it takes to actually talk to the server over the internet — this removes the extra, artificial wait the app itself used to add on top of that, not the network itself.

h: Fixed: a just-finished task could fail to save when you logged out or signed back in right after

i.x: Found a real cause of work going missing after signing back in, separate from the sync issues fixed in the last couple of updates. Logging out used to kick off one last save attempt in the background without actually waiting for it, then immediately disconnect from the cloud and sign you out. If that last save hadn't finished yet, it lost the race against the disconnect and could fail silently — with nothing on screen showing anything had gone wrong.

Logging out now actually waits for that final save to finish before disconnecting (it still won't hang forever — it gives up after a few seconds if the connection is stuck, and in that case the change is still safely queued to retry automatically next time you sign in).

Also closed a related gap: loading your data on sign-in, and on the Refresh buttons elsewhere in the app, used to be able to discard a save that hadn't been confirmed sent yet. Every one of those now re-checks for and re-sends anything not yet confirmed, not just sign-in.
This does not change how field-by-field merging, renumbering, or the quiet double-edit log work — only when the app is allowed to disconnect from the cloud.

h: Changed: same-field double-edit notice is now a quiet log, syncing is faster, and new work order numbers can be made fully collision-proof

i.x: The "Someone else changed this field around the same time" popup no longer interrupts you. It's still recorded — nothing about the safety is removed — just quietly, in a new "Recent same-field double-edits" log under Management → Storage (master account only), which you can check on your own time.

Cut the delay before a save starts syncing to other devices from about 0.7 seconds down to about 0.2 seconds, so someone opening the same record right after you save is much less likely to see the old version.

Added (optional, off until set up) true one-at-a-time work order numbering: instead of every device guessing the next number from what it can see locally, a new work order can now ask the server for a real, centrally handed-out number the moment it's created, silently upgrading from its local guess. This closes even the split-second window where two devices could show the same new number. Requires a one-time setup in the database (see below) — until that's done, this does nothing and the app behaves exactly as before.

If the one-time setup isn't done yet, or the app is offline when a work order is created, nothing breaks — it silently falls back to the existing local-guess method, still protected by the renumber-on-collision safety net from the last couple of updates.

h: Fixed: a new work order could get a duplicate number if it was renumbered while still being typed

i.x: When two people create a new work order at close to the same time, it's normal and expected for both to briefly show the same number before they've synced — that part is unavoidable without a much bigger change. The problem fixed here was what happened next: if one of those two work orders got automatically renumbered to avoid the clash while its creator still had it open and typing, that open window kept saving under the OLD number, which could bring the old number back to life as a duplicate once it synced again.

An open, still-being-typed new work order now follows along the moment it gets renumbered in the background — its number updates live on screen, and every save from then on goes to the right (new) number. No duplicate, no lost typing.

You may still briefly see the same number on two different new work orders for a second or two right after both are created — that's expected. What's fixed is that it now always resolves itself correctly into two separate, correctly-numbered work orders instead of risking a duplicate.

h: Fixed: two new work orders landing on the same number could still silently overwrite each other

i.x: Found a gap in the same-number protection added a few updates ago. It worked when two devices created new work orders and then synced directly with each other — but if your device received the other person's new work order through the live background feed FIRST (before you pressed Save on your own), it quietly treated your work order as if it were always the same record as theirs, instead of recognizing it as a separate one that happened to land on the same number. Whoever saved last ended up completely replacing the other person's work order, with no renumbering and no notice — exactly what happened with work order #132 between two devices.

Every new work order now carries its own permanent, invisible fingerprint from the moment it's created. The sync system uses that fingerprint to tell "this is genuinely the same work order" apart from "this just happens to have the same number," no matter which order the updates arrive in. Two different work orders can no longer merge into one or overwrite each other — if they land on the same number, one is automatically renumbered and you're notified, same as before.

Genuinely editing the SAME existing work order from two devices at once still works as it did in the last update: both people's changes are kept field by field, with a notice only if you both changed the exact same field.

h: New: a brand-new work order now saves itself as a draft automatically, so it can't be lost

i.x: Pressing New Work Order now immediately creates a personal draft that saves itself automatically as you type — the description, notes, services performed, everything. If you close the app, your computer restarts, or you just forget to press Cancel or Save, nothing is lost: pressing New Work Order again brings back that exact same draft, picking up right where you left off.

Each person gets their own draft — Person A's in-progress new work order never shows up for Person B, and the other way around. The draft gets a reserved work order number right away and is protected by the same cross-device sync and collision safety as any saved work order.

A draft stays invisible everywhere else — work order lists, counts and reports — until you press Save. Save turns it into a normal, fully visible work order. Pressing Cancel on a draft now discards it completely, since it was never a real work order to begin with.

Editing an existing, already-saved work order still works exactly as before: those changes are only saved when you press Save. This only changes what happens before you've saved a work order for the first time.

h: Fixed: an edit to a work order (like adding notes) could get silently wiped out by someone else's edit

i.x: If two people edited the same work order around the same time on different devices — even unrelated fields, like one person adding notes while another changed the vendor — whichever save reached the cloud second used to completely replace the other's version, silently erasing whatever the first person had just added (this is very likely what happened to a day's worth of notes going missing).

Edits are now combined field by field instead of one overwriting the whole record: if you and someone else changed different things, both changes are kept. If you both changed the exact same field to different values, you'll get a clear notice saying so, so you can check it rather than silently losing one of the changes.

h: Fixed: a work order could get silently overwritten by a same-numbered one from another device

i.x: If two people created work orders around the same time on different devices before they'd finished syncing with each other, it was possible for both to land on the same work order number. The safety net added for this a few updates ago (auto-renumbering one of them instead of letting it overwrite the other) only runs on an up-to-date app — and the stuck-update bug fixed in the last update could keep a device from ever receiving it, which is almost certainly what let this slip through.
If this ever happens again, you'll now be told about it right away: a notice names the old and new work order number so you know exactly what changed, instead of it happening silently.

Management → Storage now has a "Recover missing data from this computer" button (master account only). It checks the last saved copy on that specific computer and restores anything that's missing elsewhere — including a work order that got overwritten before this fix existed. If a recovered item's number is already taken by something else now, it comes back under a new number instead of overwriting that too.

To recover a work order that went missing before this update, run the new Recover button on the SAME computer the work order was originally created on, since that's the one computer whose saved copy still has it.

h: Fixed: auto-update could get stuck and silently stop offering new versions

i.x: The update pill/card (the one that says an update is ready to install) could stop responding to both "Restart & update" and "Later" with no explanation. The underlying cause: if applying an update ever failed to fully load, the app lost track of what version it still needed to get to and quietly stopped checking for anything newer from then on — so later updates kept piling up without ever being offered again, even though a check said everything was current.

The "Check for updates" button on the login screen could say a version was "the newest" that was actually older than what had already been downloaded and was waiting to install. It now always reports the version the app itself has confirmed, instead of whatever happened to still be on screen.
If installing an update genuinely fails, the card now says so clearly ("Update failed") instead of sitting there doing nothing when you click it, and the app will offer the update again shortly.

h: Citations: press-and-hold copy now cleans up the row for pasting into a spreadsheet

i.x: Press-and-hold copy on a Citations row now cleans the row up before it lands in your spreadsheet, instead of copying exactly what's on screen: the driver's name keeps normal capitalization with just the LAST name in caps (e.g. "Kelly CONAN"); the citation number copies alone, without the Pending/Completed/Guilty status tag next to it; the court name and address copy in normal capitalization instead of all caps (e.g. "Las Cruces Magistrate Court", "4610 Maher Ave, Laredo, Texas 78041"); the court phone number copies as plain digits with dashes only, no parentheses and no +1 (e.g. "509-674-5533"); the violation type copies as "Moving violation" or "Non-moving violation" instead of just "Moving"/"Non-Moving"; and the truck number and points both copy in bold.
This only changes what gets copied to your clipboard — the Citations table on screen looks exactly the same as before.

h: Scan Report now auto-renames the file to the citation/DVER number it read

i.x: Citations and Inspections already have a Scan Report button that reads a photo or PDF of the actual ticket or inspection report with AI and fills in the form for you. It now also renames that file for you: a citation photo becomes "Citation# 123456", and an inspection report becomes "DVER# NM123456789" — using the number it actually read off the document, instead of the camera's default file name.
If you scan two pages or photos of the same report at once (front/back, multiple pages), each file gets the same name with (1), (2), etc. so they don't overwrite each other.

This only renames files added through Scan Report. Files added the regular way (the Upload Files / Photos / Videos button) keep whatever name they came in with, since that upload doesn't read the document at all.

h: Permit Portals: quiet background check no longer pops a notice on login

i.x: Permit Portals quietly re-checks KY, NY, NM and OR shortly after the app opens, and again every couple of hours, with no window shown. If one of those states' portal pages had changed and needed re-teaching, that silent check used to pop up a "Needs you" notice anyway — which is what you were seeing on every login. It no longer interrupts you for that. The status still shows as "Needs you" on that state's row inside Permit Portals, so it isn't hidden — it just won't pop up on its own anymore.
If a state actually fails while you're using it yourself (pressing Sign in, Teach, or Get permits), the notice still pops up right away, since that's a direct result of something you just did.

h: Connection Lost notice redesigned: compact, and matches light/dark mode

i.x: The "Connection Lost" popup from the last update is now a smaller, modern card instead of a big dark box — a light card on a soft blurred background in light mode, and a black card on a darker blur in dark mode (it follows whichever mode you're already using). The animated dots are now a smaller, smoother three-dot pulse instead of blinking periods.

h: New: a full-screen 'Connection Lost' notice when the internet drops, with auto-resume

i.x: If your internet connection drops while using the app, a blurred full-screen notice now appears right away: "Connection Lost" with "Trying to reconnect..." and an Exit App button below it, so it's obvious something is wrong instead of the app just quietly failing to save.

As soon as the connection comes back, the notice switches to a green "Connection Back Online" message for a moment, then disappears on its own — you don't need to log in again or do anything, you're just back where you were.
Exit App closes the app the same way the regular close button does (prompting first if you have unsaved changes open), so you're never stuck staring at the notice with no way out.

h: New: double-click a service/part on a work order to edit it, instead of delete-and-redo

i.x: On the New/Edit Work Order screen, the services and parts list below (SERVICES PERFORMED ON THIS WORK ORDER) can now be double-clicked on any row to edit that line's service code, description, quantity and unit cost in place. Previously the only option was the × delete button, so fixing a typo meant deleting the line and re-adding it from scratch.
The × delete button on each line still works the same as before, for when you actually want to remove a line rather than correct it.

h: Fixed: a new work order from one device could silently wipe out a work order from another device

i.x: Found the cause of work orders disappearing between accounts: when two devices each created a brand-new work order around the same time, before either one had finished syncing, they could end up getting assigned the exact same work order number. When that happened, whichever one synced second silently overwrote the other — it looked like the work order was deleted, but it was actually erased by a second work order claiming the same number.

That overwrite can no longer happen. If two devices ever create different work orders that land on the same number, both are now kept — the newer one is automatically bumped to the next free number instead of erasing the older one.

Also fixed the deeper reason the numbers could drift apart in the first place: the live connection that pushes other people's changes to your screen could quietly stop working (for example after your computer slept or your wifi dropped) without reconnecting on its own, so your app kept showing old data and handing out work order numbers that were already taken. It now reconnects automatically, and also double-checks against the server every couple of minutes and whenever you switch back to the app, so your view can't drift far out of date even if the live connection hiccups.

h: Removed the new notification center — back to the one reminders bell you had before

i.x: Pulled out the new notification center added over the last few builds (the floating previews, the bell merge, the preferences screen, all of it). It wasn't stable enough and got in the way, so it's gone rather than patched further. You're back to the single reminders bell exactly as it worked before this was added, with no second icon and no floating previews.
The window open/close animation (windows growing from the button or row you clicked, and shrinking back when closed) is not part of this and is still in place, since it wasn't part of what broke.

h: Fixed: notification center became unclickable after a big backlog of reminders synced in

i.x: The first time this version ran, every existing reminder became a "new" notification at once and queued up a floating preview for each one. Those floating previews render above the notification center, so with a big backlog they ended up sitting on top of the center panel and blocking clicks on it until they all finished, which is what made it look unclickable.

Background syncing (existing maintenance reminders, driver CDL/medical expirations) now only updates the bell badge and the list silently — it no longer pops a floating preview for each one. Floating previews are reserved for things that just happened (a new work order, a completed work order, a new citation, a system error).
A floating preview will no longer appear at all while the notification center is already open, so it can't sit on top of the list and block clicks.
If the list is still unclickable after this update, close and reopen the app (or refresh the page) once — that clears any floating previews left over from before this fix.

h: Notifications now live on the one bell you already had, not a second icon

i.x: The new notification center was opening from a second bell icon added next to your existing reminders bell. There's only one bell now — clicking it opens the new notification center (preview toast, unread badge, mark read/delete, preferences), and the badge count now reflects all notifications, not just reminders.

Two "Court date" entries for the same driver with different citation numbers (e.g. WB10313 and WB10312) are two separate citation records already in your Safety data with a court date today, not a duplicate created by this update — the old reminders list would have shown both too. If one of those citations is a mistaken duplicate, use the ✕ on that row in the notification center to dismiss the notification (it won't delete the underlying citation record).

h: New: smartphone-style notification center, and windows now animate open/closed

i.x: Added a notification bell (next to the reminders bell) with a smartphone-style floating preview: a new notification slides in top-right, sits for a few seconds, then shrinks and flies into the bell with a little bounce. Click the bell to open the notification center — newest first, grouped by day, with mark read/unread, delete, mark all read and clear all.

The notification center has a preferences screen (the gear icon) to turn each kind of notification on or off: Fleet, Work Orders, Safety, Drivers, Equipment and System. Notifications are saved and stay read/unread across restarts.

Wired up real notifications right away: every existing maintenance/mileage/DOT/registration reminder, upcoming CDL and medical card expirations for active drivers, new work orders, completed work orders, and new citations. Clicking a notification opens the matching record. Duplicate notifications for the same event are not created.

Opening a window (Trucks, Work Orders, any editor, etc.) now animates from the button, tab or row you clicked, smoothly growing into place instead of just appearing. Closing a window shrinks back toward wherever it came from. This respects your system's "reduce motion" setting and never affects window dragging, resizing or the unsaved-changes prompt.

h: Permit Portals: real title bar colors, Add Permit as a real dialog, password eye, working Refresh

i.x: The minimize/maximize buttons were colored yellow/green (copied from an older, already-replaced button style). They're now plain and transparent like the rest of the app's windows — only Close is colored, matching every other window.

The + button is now a labeled "Add Permit" button styled like New Work Order and other toolbar buttons, instead of a small unlabeled icon. Pressing it opens a proper dialog window (pick trucks and permits, then Get permits / Cancel), instead of a small dropdown that could get clipped.
The print button's icon was noticeably smaller than the matching button in the Trucks list even though the button itself was the same size. The icon is now sized to match.

The password box has its own eye icon now. If you're typing a new password, it shows/hides what you typed. If the box just shows a saved password's placeholder stars, clicking the eye explains that a saved password is encrypted and can't be shown again — type a new one to replace it.

The "..." menu (Teach history, Teach buy, Portal address, Remove saved login) could render in the wrong spot after the window was dragged, because it was positioned relative to the dragged window instead of the screen. It's now moved out to the page itself when opened, so it always lands in the right place.
Added a working Refresh button next to Add Permit that re-checks every state's status without closing and reopening the window.
The hidden login fields (shown via the icon next to PASSWORD) now have small labels above each box, so it's clear what's typed even after the placeholder text is gone.

h: Permit Portals browser list: rows no longer stagger

i.x: In a browser, the OR/NY/KY/NM list in Permit Portals was centering each row's text instead of lining it up, so the state codes and names landed at a different spot on every row. The list is now left-aligned and lines up properly, with the Open portal button in its own fixed column.

h: Permit Portals in a browser: each state's portal now actually opens

i.x: Permit Portals, opened outside the TMS desktop app (a plain browser tab), used to just show a message that automatic sign-in only works in the desktop app, with no way to actually get to a portal. It now lists Oregon, New York, Kentucky and New Mexico with an Open portal button for each, which opens that state's real site in a new tab so you can sign in yourself. Fix permit files still works the same as before. Saving logins and automatic sign-in/download are still desktop-app only, since that needs the encrypted local storage and window automation only the desktop app has.

h: Permit Portals moved to the Management tab

i.x: Permit Portals is no longer on the Lists tab. It now lives on the Management tab (Permits group) instead, alongside Companies, User Accounts and the other admin tools.

h: Permit portals UI clean-up: title bar, buttons and password box

i.x: The + button's icon was effectively invisible (a plain blue square). It's now a bold white plus you can actually see.
The print button was smaller than the one in the Trucks list. It's now the same size and shape (a 30px round button) as everywhere else.

The title bar (and its minimize / maximize / close buttons) didn't match the rest of the app's windows. It now uses the exact same blue gradient and the same yellow/green/red button styling as every other window.
The password box was stretched far wider than it needed to be. It's capped to a normal width now.

Pressing the eye icon on a saved password did nothing, because the stars shown there are just a placeholder (the real password isn't loaded into the browser at all, for security) — there was nothing to reveal. The eye icon now only shows up when you're actively typing a password, where it will actually work.

h: Ctrl+A select-all, and two row-selection bugs fixed (every window)

Drag-selecting several rows, then clicking a different (unselected) row elsewhere in the same window, used to leave the old rows still highlighted instead of dropping the old selection. Clicking anywhere else in the window now always clears it first.

Drag-selecting several rows and then closing the window could leave that same selection still highlighted the next time you opened it (Trucks especially, since its list is kept in memory instead of rebuilt). Closing any window now clears its row selection first, so a fresh open never shows stale highlighted rows.

h: Permit portals: one button to get permits, hidden logins; binder warning no longer boxed in

i.x: Permit Portals: the Truck search box and the "Get permits for all trucks" button are gone. A single + button opens a picker where you check off which trucks (one, several, or all) and which permits (OR/NY/KY/NM) you want, then one Get permits button runs just those.

Permit Portals: each row's login (username) fields are now hidden behind a small icon next to PASSWORD — click it to show and edit them. The password box shows stars instead of the word "Saved" when a login is already on file.
Permit Portals: the STATE column was not lined up with the rest of its row (a 3px padding mismatch from the last redesign). It is now flush with LOGIN, PASSWORD and STATUS.
Permit Portals: the print button and the Stop button were showing the same blue gradient as Sign in instead of their own look (transparent print icon, red Stop). They now keep their intended styling.

Generate A Binder: the "some documents are missing" warning was boxed in and could get clipped inside the binder window instead of floating on top of it. It now opens as its own floating panel over the whole binder window, like it's supposed to.

h: Permit portals: progress bar with Stop, no more stacked windows, stays in the background

i.x: Get permits for all trucks now shows a progress bar (truck N of total, %) instead of just a small status line, plus a Stop button that cancels the batch (it finishes whatever it is doing for the current truck/state first, then stops).

If a state's portal window got stuck needing you (page changed, needs re-teaching), it used to pop open a brand new window for that same state on every later truck. It now skips that state for the rest of the run once its window is open, and tells you in the results list.

The automatic background check (every 2 hours) could pop a portal window on screen by itself while you were doing something else, even with Permit Portals closed, and that window could keep reappearing. It now always runs fully hidden; only a window you deliberately started with Sign in, Teach or Get permits will ever show on screen.
Closing the Permit Portals window, or pressing Stop, now actually stops the run in progress instead of leaving it to keep going (and keep opening windows) after the dialog is gone.

Redesigned to match the rest of the app: transparent minimize/maximize/close buttons on the title bar, a transparent print icon moved to the far right, a cleaner Truck search box, aligned STATE rows, and color-coded status badges (green Ready, amber Set up, red Needs you). The separate bottom Close button is gone since the X already closes it.

h: Permit portals: searchable active-truck field, simpler buttons, minimize/maximize

i.x: The Truck field is now a type-to-search box instead of a dropdown, and only lists trucks that are not marked Inactive. Typing something that is not an active truck's number clears the box instead of keeping it.

Removed the Get permits for this truck and Fix permit files buttons. Get missing permits for all trucks (now labeled Get permits for all trucks) is the one button for fetching permits; the Truck field is only used for Teach now.
Added minimize and maximize buttons next to Close, same blue title bar as before. Minimize collapses the window to just its title bar; maximize expands it to fill most of the screen.

h: Permit portals: NY OSCAR's extra login field, password eye, print button

i.x: Permit portals: New York (OSCAR) now has its own USDOT # and NYS Tax ID # boxes instead of one shared username box, since its sign-in page needs both plus the Business Type dropdown (set to Regular OSCAR automatically) before the password. Every other state is unchanged. Requires a desktop app rebuild (BUILD.bat from the latest TMS-Desktop.zip) for sign-in to use the new fields.
The password box now has the same show/hide eye as every other password field in the app, instead of being hidden by itself.
Added a Print button (the app's own print icon) next to Fix permit files.

h: Binder: Carb moved under Kingpin Axle Chart

i.x: Generate A Binder (truck window): the Carb page now sits right after Kingpin Axle Chart in the page order, instead of up near the state permit pages.

h: Binder: Kingpin Axle Chart added, after Maximum Weight Rule

h: Permit uploads no longer get a yellow highlight

i.x: Uploading a KY/NY/NM/OR Permit to a truck (including through Fix Permit Files) used to draw a yellow highlight over that truck's VIN, unit number and plate inside the saved PDF. That's turned off now - the file is saved exactly as it was, with nothing highlighted.

h: Upload dialog: the X now removes your whole selection, not just the row it's on

i.x: In the Upload documents dialog, checking several rows and then clicking the red ✕ on one of them only removed that single file, not the ones you'd checked. Clicking ✕ on a row that's part of your current selection now removes the whole selection, same as the Remove selected button. Clicking ✕ on a row you haven't checked still removes just that one file.

h: Truck Database: adding an unmatched driver to HR works again

i.x: Double-clicking a driver name in the Truck Database that was flagged "not in your system yet" showed a dead-end "view only" message instead of doing anything. That block was meant for truck fields that come from your Google Sheet; the driver link it blocked is local HR data, not a Sheet field. Double-clicking that name now asks to add the driver to HR and link them to the truck, same as before the Truck Database became view-only.

h: Upload dialog no longer jumps to the top when you check a row

i.x: In the Upload documents dialog, checking a row's checkbox (or clicking the ✕ to remove a file) redrew the whole list and reset the scroll position to the top, so on a long list you lost your place every time you selected something. The dialog now remembers and restores the scroll position across that redraw.

h: Upload dialog: skip trucks with no match, delete/select rows; phone view removed

i.x: Uploading several documents at once (drag and drop, or a multi-page permit split) no longer blocks the whole batch just because one file couldn't be matched to a truck. Files with no truck selected are now skipped, and a message after upload lists exactly which ones were skipped and why, so nothing silently goes missing and nothing silently gets attached to the wrong truck.

The Upload documents dialog now has a small red ✕ on every row to remove just that file before uploading, plus a checkbox per row and a select-all checkbox in the header to select several rows and remove them together with one Remove selected button.

The Auto / Phone / Desktop view switch (bottom-right button, or top-left on a phone) has been removed, and the app no longer switches into the phone/mobile layout at all — it is desktop-only now. This also removes the phone-layout CSS and detection code that ran on every page load.

h: Permit Portals no longer stays on top of other windows; KY auto sign-in tries harder on the consent box

i.x: Permit Portals used to always stay on top of every other window once opened, even a window you opened afterwards. It now behaves like your other windows: click another window and it comes to front, click Permit Portals and it comes back to front. Desktop app rebuild needed.

The auto sign-in's "I consent to the System Notice" step now also looks for the checkbox when it isn't wrapped in a normal label (some state portals, including KYID, lay the checkbox and its text out differently) and as a fallback will tick the one remaining unchecked box on a short sign-in step if the page clearly mentions a consent/system notice. Desktop app rebuild needed. This could not be tested against the live KYID site from here - please try it and let me know if it still doesn't tick.

h: Bulk download, select all, Esc on every window, KY permit pages no longer get skipped

i.x: Company Documents and Tax Exempt Forms: drag-select several rows (or press Ctrl+A to select all of them), then a download icon appears next to the selection count. One file downloads directly; several download together as a zip. Tax exempt forms download blank (unfilled), same as the single-form download.
Esc now closes small floating windows too (Permit Portals, Delete Documents, the upload-documents list, binder warnings), not only the main truck/driver/etc. windows.

A multi-page permit (such as a KY Vehicle Inventory PDF with one page per truck) could lose trucks: a page whose text didn't clearly show a truck's VIN/plate/unit was silently merged into whichever truck came before it instead of getting its own entry. Now only a truly blank/boilerplate page merges; a page with real content but an unreadable id gets its own entry instead of disappearing.

When a split-out permit page's own text wasn't recognized (poor text layer/OCR), it showed as "Other" and kept its page-number file name instead of becoming KY/NY/NM/OR Permit. It now also checks the original file name (e.g. "Vehicle Inventory for KYU# ...") for the same permit wording, so it's correctly named and gets the truck's row highlighted like the rest.

h: Delete Documents tool, OR Permit highlight fix, new truck default type

i.x: Management > Documents > Delete Documents (Master only): pick a document type (Registration, Annual DOT, OR/NY/KY/NM Permit) and Trucks or Trailers, see how many files match, then delete them all at once. Confirms the exact count first and cannot be undone.

The yellow highlight on a permit that lists many trucks could land on the wrong truck's row. A second, older VIN/plate source used as a fallback could carry one truck's VIN or plate onto another truck if it collided with a different truck's own VIN/plate. That fallback is now only used when a truck has no VIN/plate of its own, and never if it would collide with another truck's.
Adding a new truck now defaults Type to Conventional Sleeper instead of blank, including trucks added from FMCSA matching or from an unmatched permit.

h: Deleting a viewed file now shows the next file

i.x: In Files & Media (trucks, trailers, work orders, drivers, citations and the other file windows), deleting the file you are viewing no longer leaves it on screen. The viewer switches to the first file left in the list, or closes when none are left.

The Oregon Weight-Mile Tax enrollment page was filed as Registration 2026 because of its Registration Year column. It is now recognised as an OR Permit, and each truck listed in it gets its own OR Permit copy. Fix Permit Files also re-checks files named Registration.

h: Oregon enrollment list is recognised as an OR Permit

i.x: The Oregon Weight-Mile Tax enrollment page was filed as Registration 2026 because of its Registration Year column. It is now recognised as an OR Permit (also by the Oregon Trucking Online name and its Base Plate / Base State columns), and each truck listed in it gets its own OR Permit copy.

h: Saved portal pages no longer include the red bar or Print buttons

i.x: When a portal page is saved as a permit PDF, TMS now hides its red recording bar and the portal's own Print, Export, Clear Search and search box first, then shows them again. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: Permit Portals window matches the Trucks window, buttons easier to see

i.x: The Permit Portals title bar now uses the same blue, text size, tan symbol and red close button as the Trucks window.
The ... menu button and its menu are clearer (blue outline, bigger dots, highlighted items), and the result messages are bolder.

h: Teach: red bar always appears, old-app warning

i.x: The red recording bar could be missing if teaching was started again on a page that had been recorded before. It is now rebuilt every time, and clicks are never recorded twice.
Permit Portals warns in red when the installed desktop app is older than the page, which is what makes Teach and Get permits do nothing. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: Permit Portals: Sign in button hides once the login is saved

i.x: When a state's username and password are saved, its Sign in button is hidden. The ... menu has Open portal window if you need to look at the portal yourself. Clearing the login or typing a new password brings the button back.

h: Teaching ends after any download

i.x: The teach window now finishes and closes after any completed download, not only files named .pdf. A downloaded file with no .pdf in its name is checked and filed as a PDF if it is one. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: New TMS logo on the app icon

i.x: The TMS logo is now the icon of the Windows installer, TMS.exe, the desktop shortcut, the taskbar and the window, and of the Android launcher. Desktop and Android need a rebuild to show it.

h: Teach now shows a red recording bar

i.x: Teach looked like it did nothing because the portal's own page title replaced the TEACHING title. The portal window now shows a message when teaching starts and a red recording bar with Payment page reached, This page is the permit and Cancel buttons. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: Oregon portal: Print now works

i.x: The Oregon Trucking Online Print button said it could not open the print view. Portal windows now allow that pop-up, save the print view as a PDF and send it to TMS to file as OR Permit. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: Portal sign-in handles the consent box (KY)

i.x: Permit Portals sign-in now ticks the "I consent to the System Notice" box when a portal needs it before Next, then continues to the password step. It never ticks Remember me. Desktop app rebuild needed.

h: Fix Permit Files moved inside Permit Portals, new icon

i.x: Fix Permit Files is now a button inside the Permit Portals window, so the Lists tab has just one Permits button. In a browser the window shows that button only.
New Permit Portals icon: a browser window with a permit and a green download badge.

h: Permits group on the Lists tab in every window

i.x: The Permits group (Permit Portals, Fix Permit Files) is now always on the Lists tab. Permit Portals tells you if it is running outside the desktop app, and Fix Permit Files works anywhere.

h: Permits group now always shows on the Lists tab (desktop app)

i.x: The Permits group (Permit Portals, Fix Permit Files) did not appear on the Lists tab. It now shows for every login in the desktop app, and only the Master account can open or change anything in it.

h: Permits on the Lists tab, slim themed windows

Generate A Binder and Permit Portals now use the same slim blue title bar as your other windows, with a small title and a compact close button. Permit Portals can be dragged.
The binder's missing-documents warning is now its own window with a title bar. You can drag it, close it with the X, and it matches the app theme in light and dark mode.

h: Permit Portals: simpler window, Management tab, truck-only highlight

i.x: Permit Portals is now compact: State, Username, Password, Sign in and a ... menu (Teach history, Teach buy, Portal address, Remove saved login), plus a short status such as Ready or Set up: buy. Run now and Save are gone. Logins save by themselves when you leave a field, and the status refreshes after each teach or run.
The window now uses the app's blue title bar, classic buttons and dark mode. The show-password eye no longer overlaps the menu.
Permit Portals and Fix Permit Files moved to the Management tab (Permits group). They only appear for the Master account.
On permits that list several trucks, only that truck's own VIN, unit number and plate are highlighted in yellow, not the whole row.

h: Permit files: found by the binder, named KY Permit, truck row highlighted

i.x: The binder now finds permits that were uploaded with their original names, such as "Vehicle Inventory for KYU# 684665 - page 4.pdf". They no longer show Not found.

Fix Permit Files (Fleet ribbon, Billing group) goes through the permits already on your trucks. It reads each one, renames it to NY / KY / NM / OR Permit, highlights that truck's row in yellow, and adds the permit to every other truck it lists. A file that can't be read as a permit is left as it was.
New permit uploads (drag and drop, or from the portals) now get the yellow highlight on the truck's own row as well, so a permit that lists many trucks shows which line belongs to each one.

h: Permit Portals: check each truck's history, or buy up to the payment page

i.x: Pick a truck in Permit Portals and press Get permits for this truck. For each state that is missing the permit, it opens the portal history in a hidden window, finds that truck's row, downloads the PDF and files it under the truck as OR/NY/KY/NM Permit.pdf. There is also a button for all trucks that are missing permits.

If the truck is not in the portal history yet, the result shows a Buy button. It fills in everything in the background, then brings the portal window forward at the payment page. You type the card and confirm. After that it downloads the PDF, files it and closes the window. The app never types or stores card numbers and never clicks a pay button.

Teach now has two buttons per state: Teach history (open the history, click the download for the chosen truck) and Teach buy (fill in the purchase, then choose TMS > Payment page reached). Truck unit, VIN and plate are remembered as variables, so the same steps work for every truck. Card, password and account fields are never recorded.
The binder's missing-documents warning has a Get missing permits button for trucks that lack a state permit.
Desktop app only. Reinstall the desktop installer to get this. Each state needs one Teach for history and one for buying.

h: Permit Portals: teach it once, then it runs by itself

i.x: Permit Portals now has Teach and Run now. Teach opens the state portal: you sign in (it fills your saved login), click through to the permit and download it once. The app remembers the clicks (never your typing or passwords) and from then on repeats them in a hidden window by itself, about once a day while TMS is open. Run now does it on demand.
Permit PDFs that arrive from a background run are read, matched to the truck and saved without any dialog. Only a file that cannot be matched, or a duplicate, is skipped or shown for a quick check.

Kentucky and New Mexico pages that list several trucks are now saved to every truck on the page, like the Oregon list. Buttons that look like a payment, purchase or renewal are never recorded or clicked. If a portal asks for a captcha or code, or its pages change, the portal window opens and says what it needs.

h: Permit Portals: sign in once, permits come in by themselves

i.x: New Permit Portals button (Fleet ribbon, Master only, desktop app). Type each state's portal login once: New Mexico TAP, New York OSCAR, Kentucky Motor Carrier Portal and Oregon Trucking Online. Sign in opens that state's portal in its own window and fills your saved login. If the portal shows a captcha it stops so you can finish it. Any permit PDF you open or download there, or save with TMS > Save this page to TMS (Ctrl+S), goes straight into the upload dialog, which reads it and matches it to the truck.
Nothing is bought or paid automatically. This needs the new desktop installer (the wrapper changed); the web and Android apps do not show the button.

h: Truck Lease Agreement in the binder

h: Truck permits: Oregon, New York, Kentucky, New Mexico

h: More access for Admin accounts

Admins get the fleet tools: show or hide Samsara vehicles, the automatic odometer option, merge duplicate drivers, and the Deleted work orders view.
Admins can add and use tax exempt forms and company documents. Deleting them, deleting trucks or all drivers, and cloud file storage stay Master-only.

h: Clearer violation history in MVR / Violations

i.x: The driver's violation history is easier to read: bigger rows with a colored edge, status pills (Pending, Convicted, Dismissed, Inspection no ticket), a highlighted ticket number, and a tag showing which inspection a violation came from.

Mark convicted / Mark dismissed buttons in each ticket's details. Tickets with no court date that are over 30 days old are flagged 'likely paid', and one button marks all of them convicted after you confirm.
New Inspection violations (12 months) count on each driver, so roadside violations are tracked without being counted as state convictions.
Violations from inspections that had no ticket are no longer counted as open citations.

h: Window access follows Visible tabs

i.x: In Edit User Account, Window Access now only lists the tabs that are checked under Visible Tabs, for Admin as well as Standard accounts. Uncheck Accounting and its windows disappear from the list; check it again and they come back (earlier choices are kept).

h: Inspection violations now go to the driver's MVR / Violations

i.x: Driver-related violations on inspections (HOS, driver qualification, state/local traffic laws, drugs/alcohol, CDL) are added to that driver's MVR / Violations record. Vehicle-only ones (brakes, tires, lights) are not.
It runs once automatically for your existing inspections (master account), and again every time an inspection is saved or an FMCSA file is imported. Nothing is added twice.

New records start as Pending, so they do not count toward state points until you mark them convicted. If the inspection has a citation #, it is added as an open citation; otherwise as a closed warning.
MVR / Violations has a new button, From inspections, to run it by hand and see what will be added and which inspection drivers have no match in HR.

h: Android app support

View switch next to the version number: tap to cycle Auto, Phone or Desktop. Auto still picks by screen size; your choice is remembered on this device.

When a Files & Media window opens, its photos and PDFs start loading in the background, so by the time you press the eye they are usually ready. The viewer window now opens immediately and shows Loading… instead of making you wait.

h: Phone version

h: FMCSA card: compact view

h: Readable split names in the report table
